entry: Infraclass or division of ray-finned fishes ([[Actinopterygii|class Actinopterygii]]) that includes 96% of living fish species. Over 26,000 species range from giant [[Oarfish|oarfish]] of 7.6 m (25 ft) or more to the male [[Anglerfish|anglerfish]] *Photocorynus spiniceps*, 6.2 mm (0.24 in) long. A movable premaxilla lets them protrude their jaws to seize prey. Most use external fertilization, and some provide parental care. The [[Fishing|fishing]] industry harvests teleosts for food, some are farmed, and others are kept in [[Aquarium|aquariums]] or used in research on [[Genetics|genetics]] and [[Developmental biology|developmental biology]].

British children's television series created by Anne Wood and Andrew Davenport for the [[BBC]]. Four differently colored characters, named after the screens on their bellies, communicate mostly through gibberish. Designed to resemble toddlers, they are recognized in popular culture by their [[Antenna (radio)|antennae]]. The series won multiple BAFTA awards, and a single based on its theme song reached number 1 in the UK Singles Chart in December 1997. By October 2000, the franchise had generated over £1 billion ($1.6 billion) in merchandise sales. A rebooted series, green-lit in 2014, ran for 120 episodes, and a new version premiered on [[Netflix]] in 2022.

Telecommunications network that distributes television content from a central operation to many stations, pay television providers or, in the United States, multichannel video programming distributors. Until the mid-1980s, broadcast programming in most countries was dominated by a few terrestrial networks. Many early networks, such as the [[BBC]], [[PBS]] and [[NBC]], evolved from radio networks. Where networks broadcast identical central content, the terms "television network," "channel" and "station" are largely interchangeable in everyday use. Many North American networks are branded as "channels" because they have no affiliates and reach viewers through [[Cable television|cable]] or [[Satellite television|satellite]] providers. Networks may also rely on production companies for content, and many stations are self-owned.

Content produced for viewing on a television set, transmitted over the air, by satellite or cable, or distributed digitally on streaming platforms. Most programming is produced ahead of time, either in-house or by contract with [[Film|film]] production companies, and excludes breaking news and advertisements. An episodic show is a television series; its segments are episodes, and a show with a limited number of episodes is a miniseries. Early experimental broadcasts in the 1930s reached only a short distance from the tower, and World War II halted development. The first national live U.S. broadcast took place on September 4, 1951, and the first national color broadcast on January 1, 1954. Streaming services such as [[Netflix]] now let viewers watch programming at any time on a subscription basis.

Brittle, silver-white, mildly toxic [[Metalloid|metalloid]] with symbol Te and atomic number 52. It is chemically related to [[Selenium|selenium]] and [[Sulfur|sulfur]]. Its rarity in Earth's crust, comparable to that of platinum, is partly due to a volatile hydride that caused tellurium to be lost to space as a gas during Earth's formation. Tellurium-bearing compounds were first discovered in 1782 in a [[Gold|gold]] mine in [[Transylvania]] by Franz-Joseph Müller von Reichenstein. Martin Heinrich Klaproth named the element in 1798, after the Latin *tellus* ("earth"). It is usually recovered as a by-product of [[Copper|copper]] and lead production. Its main commercial uses are CdTe solar panels and thermoelectric devices, and [[Steel|steel]] and copper alloys, where it improves machinability.

American actor of Greek descent, noted for his bald head and deep, resonant voice. He is best known for playing Lt. Theo Kojak in the [[CBS]] crime drama *Kojak* (1973–1978) and the [[James Bond|James Bond]] villain Ernst Stavro Blofeld in *On Her Majesty's Secret Service* (1969). His films include *Birdman of Alcatraz* (1962), for which he was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor. A cover of Bread's "If" reached number one in the UK Singles Chart in 1975. He earned a psychology degree from [[Columbia University|Columbia University]] in 1946.

[[Dravidian languages|Dravidian]] language native to the Indian states of [[Andhra Pradesh]] and [[Telangana]], where it is also the official language. Spoken by about 100 million people, it is the most widely spoken Dravidian language and one of India's 22 scheduled languages. It is also spoken in [[Karnataka]], [[Tamil Nadu]], Kerala and Maharashtra, and by diaspora communities abroad. Telugu is a classical language with a recorded history of at least 2,000 years, and its literary tradition spans over a thousand years. The earliest Telugu words appear in inscriptions dated to c. 4th century BCE. The language predominates in the evolution of [[Carnatic music]], one of two main subgenres of Indian classical music.

Terrestrial habitat type in moderate climates, as defined by the World Wide Fund for Nature. Its richest and most distinctive forests occur in central [[China|China]] and eastern [[North America|North America]], with others in the Himalayas, Western and Central Europe, and Australasia. Typical structure includes a canopy of trees 30 to 61 m (100 to 200 ft) tall, a shade-tolerant understory, a shrub layer and ground cover. Northern Hemisphere broadleaves include [[Oak|oaks]], [[Beech|beeches]], [[Maple|maples]] and [[Birch|birches]], with conifers such as [[Pine|pines]], firs and spruces. Annual rainfall is typically over 600 mm (24 in), and annual average temperatures range from 3 to 23 °C (37 to 73 °F).

Main climate class in the middle latitudes, between the tropics and the polar regions. Temperate climates occur roughly 23.5° to 66.5° north and south of the Equator. They have wider temperature ranges and more distinct seasons than [[Tropical climate|tropical climates]], which usually differ mainly in precipitation. Latitude, [[Ocean current|ocean currents]], prevailing winds, continentality and altitude all shape them. The [[Köppen climate classification|Köppen classification]] defines a temperate (C) climate as having a mean temperature above −3 °C (26.6 °F) but below 18 °C (64.4 °F) in its coldest month. Subtypes include [[Humid subtropical climate|humid subtropical climates]], with long, hot, humid summers, and [[Mediterranean climate|Mediterranean]] climates, with dry summers and wet winters.

Coniferous or broadleaf forest in moist oceanic regions that receives heavy rain. Such forests occur in the Pacific Northwest of [[North America|North America]], the Appalachian region of the United States, southwestern [[South America|South America]], New Zealand, southeastern Australia, northwest Europe and Japan. Their understory is typically [[Moss|mosses]], [[Fern|ferns]] and some shrubs and berries. For North American wet forests, Alaback's definition requires annual precipitation over 140 cm (55 in) and a mean annual temperature between 4 and 12 °C (39 and 54 °F). Canopy conifers can stand 100 m or more tall, and their crowns collect most of the rain and moisture the forest takes in.

Structure reserved for worship, used for spiritual rituals such as prayer and sacrifice. The word derives from the [[Latin|Latin]] *templum*, a sacred precinct marked out by a priest, or augur, in [[Ancient Rome|Ancient Rome]]. Many extinct religions, including the [[Ancient Egyptian religion|Ancient Egyptian]] and Ancient Greek, had temples, as do active faiths such as Hinduism, Buddhism, Sikhism and Shinto, under names such as mandir, vihara and gurudwara. Temples usually house offerings to a [[Deity|deity]] and are maintained by [[Clergy|clergy]], with access often restricted to them. Hindu temples contain a garbhagriha (womb-chamber), an inner sanctum where the primary image of a deity is housed. [[Christianity|Christianity]] uses churches, [[Islam|Islam]] mosques and [[Judaism|Judaism]] synagogues.

American academic, inventor and ethologist. A prominent advocate for the humane treatment of [[Livestock|livestock]] at slaughter, she consults for the livestock industry. One of the first autistic people to document insights from her own experience of [[Autism|autism]], she was not formally diagnosed until adulthood. She has written more than 60 scientific papers on animal behavior. In 2010, [[Time (magazine)|Time]] named her in its "Heroes" category. The biographical film *Temple Grandin* (2010) won a Primetime Emmy Award and a Golden Globe.

Elevated [[Plateau|plateau]] in the Old City of [[Jerusalem|Jerusalem]], holy to [[Judaism|Judaism]] and [[Islam|Islam]]. It was the site of two successive Jewish temples. Solomon's Temple, built by King Solomon in 957 BCE, was destroyed by the Neo-Babylonian Empire in 587 BCE, though no archaeological evidence has verified it. The Second Temple, built in 516 BCE, was renovated by [[Herod the Great|Herod the Great]] and destroyed by the [[Roman Empire|Roman Empire]] in 70 CE. The plaza is dominated by the Dome of the Rock, completed in 692, and the Qibli Mosque of al-Aqsa. Its courtyard can host more than 400,000 worshippers. Israel has enforced a ban on prayer by non-Muslims under the "status quo" arrangement. The site remains a focus of the [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict|Israeli–Palestinian conflict]].

Religious and ethical directives, structured as a covenant document, that the [[Hebrew Bible|Hebrew Bible]] says God gave to [[Moses|Moses]]. The text appears in three distinct versions in the Hebrew Bible. Different traditions divide the text into ten commandments in different ways. The commandments are the foundational core of Jewish law ([[Halakha|Halakha]]), and most Christian traditions regard them as divinely authoritative. The [[Quran|Quran]] presents them as moral and legal guidance focused on monotheism, justice and righteousness. In the United States, laws passed in the 2020s in [[Texas|Texas]], [[Louisiana|Louisiana]] and [[Arkansas|Arkansas]] mandate their display, though these laws face legal challenges over church and state.

Chinese multinational technology [[Conglomerate (company)|conglomerate]] and holding company, founded in 1998 and headquartered in [[Shenzhen|Shenzhen]]. It is one of the highest-grossing multimedia companies in the world, and the world's largest video game vendor by equity investments. Its services include social networks, mobile games, [[E-commerce|e-commerce]], music, payment systems and multiplayer online games. It operates the instant messengers QQ and WeChat. Its first messenger, OICQ, was renamed QQ shortly after its 1999 release, reportedly due to a lawsuit threat from ICQ's owner [[AOL|AOL]]. The company surpassed a market value of US$500 billion in 2018, becoming the first Asian technology company to do so, and its valuation approached US$1 trillion in January 2021 before falling sharply.

Tough band of dense fibrous [[Connective tissue|connective tissue]], also called a sinew, that connects muscle to [[Bone|bone]]. It transmits the mechanical forces of muscle contraction to the skeleton while withstanding tension. Tendons, like [[Ligament|ligaments]], are made of collagen, but ligaments connect bone to bone while tendons connect muscle to bone. The adult human body has about 4,000 tendons. Collagen makes up 60–85% of a normal tendon's dry mass, mostly type I, and its fibers run parallel and are grouped into fascicles. Tendon cells, called tenocytes, synthesize the extracellular matrix that surrounds them. The whole tendon is enclosed by a fascia, and the space between it and the tendon tissue is filled with the paratenon, a fatty loose connective tissue.

Volcanic [[Island|island]], largest of the [[Canary Islands|Canary Islands]], off northwest Africa in the [[Atlantic Ocean|Atlantic Ocean]] (pop., 2026: 972,018). With an area of 2,034.38 sq km (785.48 sq mi), it is the largest island in Macaronesia. It is dominated by Teide, the highest mountain in [[Spain|Spain]]. Teide National Park is a [[UNESCO|UNESCO]] World Heritage Site, and the island supports many endemic species. Its capital, [[Santa Cruz de Tenerife|Santa Cruz de Tenerife]], shares capital status with [[Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] de Gran Canaria. Tourism is a major part of the economy.

All-encompassing God of Heaven in the traditional religions of [[Turkic peoples|Turkic]], Mongolic and other nomadic peoples. Worship of Tengri, called Tengrism, involves ancestor worship, [[Shamanism|shamanism]], [[Animism|animism]] and totemism. Its core beings are the Sky Father and the Earth Mother. Tengri was the national god of the [[Göktürks|Göktürks]], whose khans based their power on a mandate from him. The name is recorded in Chinese annals from the 4th century BC, describing the beliefs of the [[Xiongnu|Xiongnu]]. It is generally assumed the term originally meant "sky." Tengri was the chief deity of the ruling class of Central Asian steppe peoples from the 6th to 9th centuries.

American playwright and screenwriter, among the three foremost playwrights of 20th-century American drama with [[Arthur Miller|Arthur Miller]] and Eugene O'Neill. He wrote his first play in 1930, but his career took off with *The Glass Menagerie* (1944). *A Streetcar Named Desire* (1947), *Cat on a Hot Tin Roof* (1955), *Sweet Bird of Youth* (1959) and *The Night of the Iguana* (1961) were also successful and widely acclaimed. His later work, in a new style, appealed less widely to audiences. Much of his work was adapted to film, and he also wrote short stories, poetry, essays and a volume of memoirs. Critics agree he drew on his dysfunctional family in much of his writing. He was inducted into the American Theater Hall of Fame in 1979.

Landlocked southeastern [[United States|U.S.]] state, admitted to the Union as the 16th state on June 1, 1796 (pop., 2024: 7.22 million). Nashville is its capital and largest city. Tennessee was the last state to secede from the Union and join the Confederacy in the [[American Civil War|American Civil War]], and the first former Confederate state readmitted afterward. Federal investment in the Tennessee Valley Authority and in Oak Ridge, built for the [[Manhattan Project|Manhattan Project]], helped shift its economy from agriculture to a more diversified base. The state has been central to [[Country music|country]], [[Blues|blues]] and [[Rock and roll|rock and roll]] music. The [[Great Smoky Mountains National Park|Great Smoky Mountains]] lie in the east.

[[Synthetic element|Synthetic]] superheavy element with symbol Ts and atomic number 117. It is named after the U.S. state of [[Tennessee|Tennessee]], where key research institutions involved in its discovery are located. Its discovery was announced in Dubna, Russia, in April 2010 by a Russian–American collaboration, making it the most recently discovered element. The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry recognized it in 2015, and the name was adopted in November 2016. Tennessine may lie in the [[Island of stability|island of stability]], though its atoms have lasted only tens to hundreds of milliseconds. It is expected to be a member of the [[Halogen|halogens]] and may be a volatile metal.

Racket sport played as singles, between two opponents, or as doubles, between two teams of two players each. Players strike a hollow rubber ball covered with [[Felt|felt]] over a net into the opponent's court, aiming to make a valid return impossible. The original forms developed in France in the late Middle Ages, and the word probably comes from the French *tenez* ("receive!"), a server's call to the opponent. The modern game originated in [[Birmingham|Birmingham]], England, in the late 19th century as lawn tennis. [[Henry VIII|Henry VIII]] was a fan of its indoor precursor, now called real tennis. The four [[Grand Slam (tennis)|Grand Slam]] tournaments are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open, and tennis has been part of the [[Summer Olympic Games|Summer Olympic Games]] since 1988.

Mexica city-state on an island in Lake Texcoco, and capital of the expanding [[Aztec Empire|Aztec Empire]] in the 15th century. Its founding date is uncertain; 13 March 1325 was chosen in 1925 to mark the 600th anniversary. At its peak it was the largest city in the pre-Columbian Americas, covering an estimated 8 to 13.5 sq km (3.1 to 5.2 sq mi). Causeways and bridges linked it to the mainland, and canals allowed canoes to move throughout the city. A [[Levee|levee]], reputedly designed by Nezahualcoyotl, was completed c. 1453 and kept fresh spring water apart from the brackish lake. Tenochtitlan was captured by Tlaxcaltec and Spanish forces in 1521, after which it became a *cabecera* of the Viceroyalty of [[New Spain|New Spain]]. Its ruins lie in the historic center of [[Mexico City|Mexico City]].

Type of [[Bowling|bowling]] in which a bowler rolls a ball down a lane toward ten pins arranged in an equilateral triangle. The goal is to knock down all ten pins with the first delivery (a strike) or, failing that, the second (a spare). The lane is 60 feet (18 m) long and 41.5 inches (105 cm) wide, bordered by gutters. Oil on roughly the first two-thirds of the lane lets the ball skid before it hooks into the pins. The sport arose in the early 1800s as an alternative to nine-pin bowling, and standardized regulations were agreed only near the end of that century. After automated mechanical pinsetters, it enjoyed a "golden age" in the mid-20th century. Since the 1980s, declining television ratings and league participation have pushed centers to become entertainment venues.

Algebraic object describing a multilinear relationship between sets of objects associated with a [[Vector space|vector space]]. Tensors may map between vectors, scalars and other tensors, and include dual vectors and the dot product. They are important in [[Physics|physics]], in [[Mechanics|mechanics]] (stress, elasticity, fluid mechanics) and in [[General relativity|general relativity]] (stress–energy and curvature tensors). Tullio Levi-Civita and Gregorio Ricci-Curbastro popularized tensors in 1900, continuing earlier work by [[Bernhard Riemann|Bernhard Riemann]]. A tensor field is a tensor that varies across space, as the stress within an object may. Tensors can be represented as multidimensional arrays of components, and the number of indices gives the tensor's order or rank.
